Section(s): 5. A process engineering example

Text and equations in reading order:
    We propose two models to describe the system. Two differential equations, common to both models, describe the component balances within the reactor:
(16.1) \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{1}}{\mathrm{d}t} =(r-u_{1}-\theta_{4})x_{1}    [code: ODE, computes x_{1}, code proposes balance]
(16.2) \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{2}}{\mathrm{d}t} =-\frac{rx_{1}}{\theta_{3}}+u_{1}(u_{2}-x_{2})    [code: ODE, computes x_{2}, code proposes balance]
    The first model assumes Monod-type kinetics for substrate consumption, giving a third model equation:
(17) M_{I}(\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathbf{u},t);\quad r=\frac{\theta_{1}x_{2}}{\theta_{2}+x_{2}}    [code: algebraic, computes ?, code proposes constitutive]
    The second model assumes Canoid-type kinetics and thus, instead of Eq. (17), gives the model form:
(18) M_{I I}(\pmb{\theta},\mathbf{u},t)\colon\quad r=\frac{\theta_{1}x_{2}}{\theta_{2}x_{1}+x_{2}}    [code: algebraic, computes ?, code proposes constitutive]
    The experimental conditions that characterise a particular experiment are: (i) the initial biomass concentration (or inoculation), $ x_0^0 $, with range 1–10 g l $ ^{-1} $; (ii) the dilution factor, $ u_1 $, with range 0.05–0.20 h $ ^{-1} $; (iii) the substrate concentration in the feed, $ u_2 $, with range 5–35 g l $ ^{-1} $. The initial substrate concentration, $ x_2(0) $, is always 0.01 g l $ ^{-1} $ and cannot be manipulated for experiment design purposes. Both $ x_1 $ and $ x_2 $ can be measured during the experiment ( $ y = [x_1, x_2]^T $).

Symbols:
  x_{1}: Measured concentration x₁. (computed)
  r: Specific growth rate appearing in the biomass balance and kinetic law. [h^-1] (computed)
  u_{1}: Dilution factor. [h^-1] (variable)
  \theta_{4}: First-order biomass loss-rate constant in the biomass balance. [h^-1] (parameter)
  x_{2}: Substrate concentration. [g l^-1] (computed)
  \theta_{3}: Yield coefficient relating biomass growth to substrate consumption. [-] (parameter)
  u_{2}: Substrate concentration in the feed. [g l^-1] (variable)
  M_{I}: Model I, using the Monod-type substrate-consumption kinetic law. (computed)
  \theta: Vector of model parameters. (computed)
  u: Vector of time-varying process controls or inputs. (computed)
  \theta_{1}: Kinetic rate parameter in the numerator of the substrate-consumption rate law. (parameter)
  \theta_{2}: Kinetic denominator parameter; it is the Monod saturation parameter and multiplies biomass in the Canoid denominator. (parameter)
  M_{II}: Model with Canoid-type kinetics. (computed)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Monod-type kinetics for substrate consumption
  - Canoid-type kinetics

Laws: 16.1, 16.2, 17, 18
